title: Lesson 4: BLESS - Serve with Loving Sacrifice
description: Before Jesus asked His friends to serve, He knelt and washed their feet. This lesson shows you how to serve your one from freedom, not for approval, with a simple pattern from that night: rise, lay aside, and kneel.

blocks.text: In Lessons 2 and 3 you prayed for your one, listened, and opened your table. You are blessed to be a blessing, and each of those rhythms has been building something: a real friendship with your one. Now comes the most hands-on rhythm of the five. Serving is where love stops only showing up and starts rolling up its sleeves.

blocks.alt: Jesus kneeling with a basin and a towel, washing the feet of His disciples at the Last Supper

blocks.title: The Towel and the Basin
blocks.text:
It was the night before the cross. Jesus knew exactly what was coming: Judas would betray Him, Peter would deny Him, and the rest would scatter. Nobody at the table had washed anyone's feet. It was the lowest job in the house, and no one wanted it.

"Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going back to God, rose from supper. He laid aside his outer garments, and taking a towel, tied it around his waist. Then he poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet." (John 13:3-5)

Peter could not stand it. "You shall never wash my feet." Jesus answered, "If I do not wash you, you have no part with me." When He was finished, He sat back down and said, "If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet." (John 13:14)

Jesus had every right to be served, but He chose to serve. He had hours left to live, and He spent them on dirty feet. That is the picture He wanted His followers to keep: not power, not status, but a towel and a basin.
Let Him Wash You First

Before Jesus told anyone to wash feet, He washed theirs, and Peter nearly missed the whole point. He wanted to be the one who served. Jesus told him that unless he let himself be washed, he had no part with Him. You cannot wash anyone's feet until you let Jesus wash yours.

That is the gospel in a basin. Jesus knelt for you at the cross and washed away what you could never scrub off yourself. So you do not serve to earn your place with God or to prove you are a good person. Your debt is paid. Your standing is settled. You have nothing left to prove, so you can wash someone's feet without needing them to wash yours back.
For you were called to freedom, brothers. Only do not use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love serve one another.
4.1 - What changes when you serve as someone Jesus has already served?
Greatness, Upside Down
A few days earlier, the mother of James and John had asked Jesus to seat her sons at His right and left in His kingdom. The other ten heard and got angry. Jesus called them all together.

You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them. It shall not be so among you. But whoever would be great among you must be your servant, and whoever would be first among you must be your slave, even as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.

The world measures greatness by how many people serve you. Jesus measures it by how many people you serve. The world counts followers; Jesus counts feet washed. The world says climb; Jesus says kneel. In His kingdom the way down is the way up.
4.2 - Where are you most tempted to measure greatness the way the world does?
Rise, Lay Aside, Kneel
Look again at what Jesus did in John 13. He rose from supper, He laid aside His outer garments, and He knelt to wash. Those three moves give you a simple pattern for serving your one.

blocks.title: Rise, Lay Aside, Kneel
content: Rise. Get up from your seat and move toward a need. Start with a need you have already heard from your one. In Lesson 3 you learned to ask, ask again, and remember. Serving is what you do with what you remembered.
Lay aside. Set down whatever is in the way: your schedule, your comfort, your right to be served, and your wish to be thanked.
Kneel. Do one specific, humble thing that meets the need, and expect nothing back.

blocks.text: Picture a neighbor who mentions over coffee that her husband's back surgery means the leaves will sit in the yard all fall. On Saturday morning, a rake is already going in her yard. Nobody made a speech, and nobody asked for anything in return. That is a towel and a basin on an ordinary street.

Notice that the most loving offers are specific. "Let me know if you need anything" is kind, but it hands the work back to the person who is already struggling. "Can I bring dinner Thursday?" or "I have Saturday morning free. Can I help with the yard?" gives them something easy to say yes to.
4.3 - What need have you heard from your one, and what is one specific way you could meet it?
This Week's Practice

Pick one need you have heard from your one. Rise, lay aside, and kneel: make one specific offer this week, follow through, and expect nothing back. If you have not heard a need yet, go back to Listen first and ask your one, "How can I help this week?"
4.4 - How would you explain to a friend why you serve without needing anything back?
Lesson 4 Review

On His last night, the King knelt with a towel and a basin. Before He asks you to wash anyone's feet, Jesus washes yours, so you serve from freedom, not for approval. In His kingdom, greatness is measured by whose feet you wash. You are blessed to be a blessing, so serve your one the way He served you: rise, lay aside, and kneel, starting with the need you heard.
In the next lesson, you will learn the last rhythm, Story: how to share your own story and the story of Jesus with your one.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
The BLESS rhythms are adapted from BLESS: 5 Everyday Ways to Love Your Neighbor and Change the World by Dave Ferguson and Jon Ferguson.
